rules.prompt: a person lifting or carrying a load with a bent back instead of bent knees
a person bending deeply forward at the waist or twisting their trunk while reaching into a car door
a person working with one or both hands raised above shoulder height
a person holding an awkward or strained arm or wrist posture while fitting a part or using a tool

segments.description: A person is walking across a large, rectangular safety mat in a workshop.
A person is walking while pushing a cart containing a blue bin in a workshop.
A person is working on a car door frame in a factory setting.
A worker is assembling a car door on a mobile workstation in a factory setting.
A person is working on a car door frame in a factory setting.

lss.summary: The workstation WS10 exhibits significant transportation waste, accounting for 52% of the observed time. The operator spends a substantial portion of the cycle moving materials, which disrupts value-adding assembly tasks. No safety violations were observed.

lss_cards.title: Implement material delivery system
lss_cards.observation: Operator spends 26 seconds per cycle transporting materials, specifically observed between 00:02-00:18 and 00:30-00:40.

evidence.note: Operator pushing cart with blue bin.

lss_cards.root_cause: Materials are not delivered to the point of use, forcing the operator to leave the workstation.
lss_cards.recommendation: Introduce a water spider or flow rack system to deliver parts directly to the assembly area, allowing the operator to remain at the workstation.

lss_cards.title: Optimize workstation layout
lss_cards.observation: Operator walks 2 seconds at the start of the cycle.
lss_cards.root_cause: Workstation layout requires unnecessary movement to reach the starting position.
lss_cards.recommendation: Rearrange the station into a compact cell to minimize walking distance.

operator_questions.question: I noticed you moving the mobile workstation at 00:30. Is this movement required for every assembly, or could the parts be staged closer?

knowledge_cards_used.title: Replace manual carrying with flow racks or a water spider
knowledge_cards_used.source: T. Ohno, Toyota Production System (seven wastes); J. Liker, The Toyota Way (flow, standardized material delivery)

knowledge_cards_used.title: Reduce transfer batch size and distance
knowledge_cards_used.source: M. Rother and J. Shook, Learning to See (value stream flow); T. Ohno, Toyota Production System

knowledge_cards_used.title: Bring parts and tools into the normal working area
knowledge_cards_used.source: R. M. Barnes, Motion and Time Study: Design and Measurement of Work (principles of motion economy)

knowledge_cards_used.title: Shorten walking with a compact cell layout
knowledge_cards_used.source: T. Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (seven wastes); ECRS method of work simplification

knowledge_cards_used.title: Use both hands and fixtures instead of holding
knowledge_cards_used.source: R. M. Barnes, Motion and Time Study (principles of motion economy)

knowledge_cards_used.title: ECRS review of every non-value-adding element
knowledge_cards_used.source: ECRS method of work simplification (industrial engineering practice); R. M. Barnes, Motion and Time Study

knowledge_cards_used.title: Confirm the root cause on the shop floor with 5 Whys
knowledge_cards_used.source: T. Ohno, Toyota Production System (5 Whys); J. Liker, The Toyota Way (genchi genbutsu)
